analysis:
Examined all supplied metadata, BASE/HEAD source and patches for three test files against the canonical index and detailed T-041. No independently supported security regression appears in these test changes. SSDCheckpointMaintenanceEpochTests.swift HEAD 83–90 now ages both persisted mtime and in-memory last-hit accounting before TTL retirement; survivor reuse and unchanged epoch assertions remain. SSDCheckpointRecencyCoordinationTests.swift HEAD 99–139 replaces serialized reads with shared access, requires exclusive upgrade for mutation, and checks that overlapping authenticated snapshots remain identical while later touches invalidate old identities. Its external replacement and ciphertext-corruption rejection tests remain at 143–160. SSDHybridCheckpointCoordinationTests.swift patch HEAD 33–71 tests overlapping stages, deferred recency refresh and reauthentication of outdated receipts; added tests at 123–234 exercise writer precedence, retirement/scan exclusion and sole-reader corrupt-file deletion. HEAD 273–276 checks cancellation leaves no holder or waiter. These concern A-001, TB-007 and T-041 confidentiality/integrity and T-016 availability; no changes to wire authorization, attestation, billing, account scoping, key derivation or encryption format are visible.
Integration must verify these expectations against SSDCheckpointFileCoordinator, SSDHybridCheckpointStore and maintenance implementations: atomic upgrade/downgrade and alias coordination, writer fairness, cancellation cleanup, bounded concurrent staging reservations, identity revalidation under exclusive donation access, and TTL accounting when overlapping readers skip persisted touches, including multiple stores/restarts. Production implementations and fixture changes are outside this batch; tests express contracts rather than establish their enforcement. Preserve this material implementation uncertainty for integration, without treating missing source as a vulnerability.
